Your Mission

In this new project, you will learn about buzzers in Arduino and the difference between active and passive buzzers.

At the end, you will build a circuit that plays music with a button. You will write all your answers and explanations in the Buzzer Activity document.

How This Project Works

Watch. Answer. Simulate. Build.

  1. Make your copy of the Buzzer Activity template.
  2. Watch the video and answer Questions 1 to 5 in your document.
  3. Build the circuit in Tinkercad using the diagram your teacher gives you.
  4. Show the working simulation to the teacher.
  5. Receive the materials and build the circuit in real life.
  6. Complete Part 2 of your document and turn it in.

IMPORTANT → You will not receive a buzzer until your Tinkercad version is complete, working, and checked by the teacher.

Part 1 · Active vs. Passive Buzzers

A buzzer is an output, just like an LED. Instead of light, it makes sound. There are two kinds, and they do not work the same way.

Video: How to Use Buzzers with an Arduino

  • 01Watch the video.Pay attention to how each buzzer is connected, its polarity, and the code used to make sound.
  • 02Answer Questions 1 to 5 in your document.Write each answer in the box under the question.

The Questions

  • Q1What is the main difference between active and passive buzzers as discussed in the video?
  • Q2How do you connect an active buzzer to an Arduino?Describe the process briefly.
  • Q3Explain why the polarity of an active buzzer is important.What happens if you connect it incorrectly?
  • Q4How can you control the sound produced by a passive buzzer using an Arduino?Include the command mentioned in the video.
  • Q5According to the video, what is a limitation of using the tone command with multiple buzzers?

THINK ABOUT IT → If you want to play a melody with different notes, which buzzer do you need? Why?

Part 2 · Practice: Music With a Button

Build a circuit that plays any music sound. Use a push button as a switch: press it once to turn the music on, press it again to turn it off.

Diagram and code: use the circuit diagram and the code explanation below. Click any image to see it bigger.

  • 01Study the diagram.Find the pin for the button, the pin for the buzzer, and where each part connects to GND.
  • 02Build the circuit in Tinkercad first.Use one Arduino, one breadboard, one push button, and one buzzer. In Tinkercad the buzzer is called Piezo.
  • 03Write your code.Start from the example below. It plays the song when you press the button. Change the song and make the button turn the music on and off. Use tone() to play notes and make the button turn the music on and off.
  • 04Run the simulation.The button must turn the music on and off correctly before you continue.
  • 05Show your Tinkercad circuit to the teacher.After approval, you will receive the materials for the physical build.
  • 06Build the same circuit in real life.Use the same pins and code you already tested.
  • 07Complete Part 2 of your document.Add your clickable Tinkercad share link, screenshots, photos, materials, connections, your code, and your code explanation.

YOUR CHALLENGE → How can the Arduino remember if the music is on or off between button presses?
